Code review confirms all new features properly implemented. CRITICAL pre-existing finding: csrf-token cookie is never issued by the server, making ALL buyer POST API calls (including the new upgrade button) return 403 CSRF_INVALID in production.

critical.issue: csrf-token cookie is NEVER set by the server. proxy.ts validates CSRF (requires X-CSRF-Token header == csrf-token cookie) but no code in the app issues the csrf-token cookie. Authenticated buyer POST calls never include X-CSRF-Token header. Result: ALL buyer POST API calls return 403 CSRF_INVALID in production. This is PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by this iteration) but directly breaks the new plan upgrade button. Affects: shortlist, requests, prequal, plan upgrade, etc.

integration_issues.issue: PlanUpgradeCard.tsx fetches POST /api/buyer/plan/upgrade without X-CSRF-Token header. csrf-token cookie is never set. → 403 CSRF_INVALID response. Upgrade will silently fail (error state shows 'Upgrade failed. Please try again.'). Fix: either issue csrf-token cookie on buyer session init + set header in fetch, or add /api/buyer/plan/upgrade to CSRF exempt list in proxy.ts.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix CSRF token flow — either: (A) generate and set csrf-token cookie server-side (e.g., in proxy.ts via response.cookies.set) and read it client-side to include as X-CSRF-Token header; OR (B) add /api/buyer/* to CSRF-exempt routes in proxy.ts (less secure but simpler); OR (C) implement useCsrf() hook that reads the cookie and injects header into all fetch calls. This pre-existing bug blocks ALL buyer POST API actions including the new plan upgrade.

rca_of_the_issue.title: CSRF token never issued — all buyer POST API calls fail with 403
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: 1. Click 'Upgrade to Premium' button in buyer dashboard. 2. POST /api/buyer/plan/upgrade sent without X-CSRF-Token header. 3. proxy.ts validateCsrfToken() checks: csrfHeader=null, csrfCookie=null → returns false → 403 CSRF_INVALID. 4. PlanUpgradeCard.tsx error handler shows 'Upgrade failed. Please try again.'
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: proxy.ts validates CSRF for all mutating API routes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) to /api/* that are not webhooks, cron, /api/admin/auth/, /api/auth/, or /api/public/. However, no code in the app ever sets the csrf-token cookie. The browser never receives the cookie, so it can never be included in subsequent requests. Additionally, frontend fetch calls never include X-CSRF-Token header. Both conditions must be true for CSRF to pass.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Option A (Recommended): In proxy.ts, generate a secure random csrf-token on GET requests for authenticated portals and set it via response.cookies.set('csrf-token', token, {httpOnly: false, sameSite: 'strict'}). Then create a useCsrf() React hook that reads document.cookie for csrf-token and adds it as X-CSRF-Token header to all fetch calls. Option B (Quick fix): Add /api/buyer/plan/upgrade to CSRF-exempt list in proxy.ts (also add other buyer POST routes). Option C: Remove CSRF validation entirely and rely on Supabase session for auth (sameSite cookies provide CSRF protection natively in modern browsers).
